localized.title: Valley Valentines Event
localized.guidance:
Love is officially in the air: Our Valley Valentines event is on from now until February 25.
Complete daily quests for some of the Valley's most iconic sweethearts, and earn exclusive rewards. You'll receive seasonal furniture, a photo frame for your Royal Phone, and even enchanted floating rose petals for an extra-romantic atmosphere!

localized.title: Évé­ne­ment Valen­tins de la vallée
localized.guidance:
L'amour est offi­ciel­le­ment dans l'air<nbsp>: notre évé­ne­ment Valen­tins de la val­lée se déroule dès main­te­nant et jusqu'au 25 février.
Accom­plis les quêtes quo­ti­diennes pour cer­tains des couples les plus emblé­ma­tiques de la val­lée et gagne des récom­penses exclu­sives. Tu rece­vras des meubles sai­son­niers, un cadre photo pour ton télé­phone royal et même des pétales volants de rose enchan­tée pour une ambiance encore plus romantique<nbsp>! À bien­tôt dans la vallée<nbsp>!

localized.title: Evento L'amore è nella valle
localized.guidance:
L'amore è uffi­cial­mente nell'aria: il nos­tro evento L'amore è nella valle è in corso fino al 25 feb­braio.
Com­pleta le mis­sioni gior­na­liere per alcuni degli inna­mo­rati più famosi della valle e ottieni premi esclu­sivi. Rice­ve­rai oggetti d'arre­da­mento sta­gio­nali, una cor­nice foto­gra­fica per il tuo tele­fono regale e per­sino dei petali di rosa flut­tuanti incan­tati per un'atmo­s­fera ancora più romantica!

localized.title: Event „Valen­tins­tag im Tal“
localized.guidance:
Die Liebe liegt offi­zi­ell in der Luft! Unser Valen­tins­tags­event läuft ab heute bis zum 25. Februar.
Schließe täg­li­che Auf­ga­ben für einige der bekann­tes­ten Lie­bes­paare ab und hole dir tolle Beloh­nun­gen. Dazu gehö­ren sai­so­nale Möbel, ein Foto­rah­men für dein herr­schaft­li­ches Tele­fon und sogar ver­zau­berte flie­gende Rosen­blät­ter für eine beson­ders roman­ti­sche Atmosphäre!

localized.title: Evento San Valen­tín en el valle
localized.guidance:
¡Lo que nece­si­tas es amor! Ya está dis­po­ni­ble el evento San Valen­tín en el valle, que durará hasta el 25 de febrero.
Com­pleta misio­nes dia­rias rela­cio­na­das con algu­nos de los tor­to­li­tos más emble­má­ti­cos del valle y podrás ganar recom­pen­sas exclu­si­vas. Reci­bi­rás mue­bles de tem­po­rada, un marco de fotos para tu telé­fono real e incluso péta­los de rosa para crear un ambiente de lo más romántico.

localized.title: <nobr>「バレー</nobr>​<nobr>バレンタイン」</nobr>​<nobr>イベント</nobr>
localized.guidance:
<nobr>いよいよ愛のシーズンが到来！</nobr>​<nobr>只今、</nobr>​<nobr>「バレー</nobr>​<nobr>バレンタイン」</nobr>​<nobr>イベントが</nobr>​<nobr>2月25日まで開催中です！
バレーで最もアイコニックな</nobr>​<nobr>恋人たちの</nobr>​<nobr>デイリー</nobr>​<nobr>クエストを</nobr>​<nobr>クリアして、</nobr>​<nobr>季節に</nobr>​<nobr>ちなんだ</nobr>​<nobr>家具や、</nobr>​<nobr>王家のスマホで</nobr>​<nobr>セルフィーを</nobr>​<nobr>一層</nobr>​<nobr>輝かせる</nobr>​<nobr>フレーム、</nobr>​<nobr>とびきり</nobr>​<nobr>ロマンティックな</nobr>​<nobr>宙を舞う</nobr>​<nobr>バラの花びらと</nobr>​<nobr>いった</nobr>​<nobr>限定報酬を</nobr>​<nobr>ゲット</nobr>​<nobr>しましょう！</nobr>

localized.title: 星谷情人节赛事
localized.guidance:
爱意满谷，甜蜜官宣：星谷情人节赛事现已开启，持续至2月25日。
完成星谷中一众经典甜蜜爱侣的每日专属任务，赢取专属奖励。你会获得赛季家具和皇家手机专属相框，甚至还有魔法漂浮玫瑰花瓣，为你打造浪漫满溢的氛围！

localized.title: Evento de Dia de São Valentim do Vale
localized.guidance:
O amor está oficialmente no ar: nosso evento de Dia de São Valentim no Vale já está acontecendo e fica até dia 25.
Complete Missões Diárias para alguns dos mais icônicos casais do Vale e ganhe prêmios exclusivos. Você receberá mobília sazonal, uma moldura de fotos para seu Telefone Real e até pétalas flutuantes encantadas para uma atmosfera extra romântica!

systems.title: Quest and Mission Progression
systems.summary: Quests are DDV’s structured story and activity progression. Each Quest can contain Steps, SubSteps, and Objectives, and its page keeps the official objective text separate from any additional Wand guidance.
systems.availability: A Quest may be not started, in progress, or completed. Unlock conditions vary by Quest, so use the requirements shown on that Quest’s page rather than assuming a universal rule.
actions: Follow the current Step, SubStep, and Objectives in order.
Search by a localized Quest name to reach the same canonical Quest page.
mechanics: Official Quest instructions remain the canonical task text. Curated guidance is added only where the official wording leaves a puzzle, target, or sequence unclear.
Known problems and workarounds are linked through Guide > Issues instead of being mixed into the Quest instructions.
warnings: Completing a Quest does not necessarily mean every world object associated with it becomes ordinary removable decoration.

systems.title: Star Paths
systems.summary: Star Paths are structured limited-time progression tracks built from Duties and Routine Duties. Wand presents them as a searchable guide rather than recreating the in-game screen.
systems.availability: Availability and duty sets are tied to the verified Star Path occurrence. Use the occurrence dates shown on the specific Star Path page.
actions: Review Duties and Routine Duties and their localized text.
Use curated duty guidance when the official wording is ambiguous.
mechanics: Current duty denominators and localization are versioned by occurrence.
Historical or future Star Path data is not inferred from recurring patterns.
warnings: Do not assume an old duty list applies to a later Star Path.

systems.title: Astronomer's Journey
systems.summary: Astronomer's Journey is a current v1.25 introductory Star Path flow with 15 Duties and 3 Routine Duties across one week.
systems.availability: It belongs to the current v1.25 onboarding/FTUE flow and is tracked separately from the normal seasonal Star Path occurrence.
actions: Follow its Quest flow and complete the 15 Duties and 3 Routine Duties shown on the current Guide page.
Use the localized duty text and curated explanations where a duty is ambiguous.
mechanics: Its duty set is a distinct current flow rather than a reusable template for seasonal Star Paths.
warnings: Do not assume these Duties apply to a different Star Path or game version.

systems.title: Events and Event Board
systems.summary: Events are persistent Guide entities with verified occurrences. Wand separates the event itself, occurrence history, and whether the event is practically accessible now.
systems.availability: Each Event page reports verified occurrence dates and a separate ACCESSIBLE_NOW / NOT_ACCESSIBLE_NOW / UNKNOWN state when an event-specific accessibility gate is known.
actions: Browse current and past verified occurrences.
Use the Event page for canonical guidance and linked Issues; community Tips remain separate.
mechanics: One Event can have multiple verified occurrences.
Past occurrences remain visible instead of being overwritten by the latest window.
warnings: A repeating cadence is not evidence of a missing occurrence or exact start/end date.

systems.title: Dreamlight Duties
systems.summary: Dreamlight Duties are player-facing duties that contribute to normal Dreamlight progression. The current v1.25 data model treats duty definitions and their rewards as structured game data.
systems.availability: Duty availability depends on current game state and definition conditions; this page does not invent a universal unlock point.
actions: Complete the active duty requirement shown by the game.
Use Wand data to identify the canonical duty definition and related reward/resource when available.
mechanics: Duty definitions are separate from Star Path Duties even when the UI language is similar.
warnings: Do not mix seasonal Star Path requirements with normal Dreamlight Duties.

systems.title: Collection Discovery
systems.summary: Collection discovery records whether canonical game items/entities have been discovered or collected under the current game semantics. Wand Collection is broader than the game’s native Collection tabs.
systems.availability: Collection entries are available in Wand from the current versioned database; save-backed state is optional.
actions: Browse by Wand Collection family, World, Universe, tags, and other supported facets.
Load a compatible save to add personal collected/unlocked state where the semantic model supports it.
mechanics: Collection membership/discovery and inventory ownership are separate semantics.
Raw internal definitions that are not suitable for public browse are suppressed or labeled with reviewed structural labels.
warnings: A Collection entry does not imply the item is currently obtainable or individually purchasable.

systems.title: Backpack Inventory
systems.summary: The backpack is the player-carried inventory surface backed by the game’s ListInventory/ownership routing. Wand treats its current v1.25 ownership semantics separately from Collection discovery.
systems.availability: Inventory state is save-backed; Wand can only show personal quantities when a compatible save is loaded.
actions: Use item identity and quantity data to inspect carried resources.
Move items through normal in-game inventory/storage interactions when playing.
mechanics: Ownership routing is data-driven through current ListInventory compatibility semantics.
warnings: Do not infer entitlement or premium ownership from a local inventory quantity alone.

systems.title: Storage Chests
systems.summary: Storage chests provide persistent container storage separate from the player backpack. Current v1.25 evidence distinguishes container inventories from player-carried inventory.
systems.availability: Individual storage access depends on the chest/container and the current save state.
actions: Store and retrieve supported inventory items through the chest/container interface.
Use Wand read-only save context to distinguish container contents from backpack contents when available.
mechanics: Container inventory identity must be preserved; Wand does not flatten every stored item into the backpack.
warnings: Capacity and upgrade details are container-specific and are not generalized without exact evidence.

systems.title: Scrooge McDuck's Store
systems.summary: Scrooge McDuck's Store is the normal in-game store/catalog system for rotating and catalog-based goods. It is separate from the Premium Shop.
systems.availability: What is available depends on the player’s current Store state and the applicable in-game catalog rules.
actions: Check the current Store inventory/catalog for normal in-game purchases.
Use Collection or item pages to distinguish Store provenance from Premium Shop provenance.
mechanics: Scrooge Store state and Premium Shop LiveOps offers are separate systems and should be shown separately.
warnings: Do not use Premium Shop rotation information as a substitute for Scrooge Store availability, or vice versa.

systems.title: Premium Shop Purchase Units
systems.summary: Premium Shop offers are LiveOps purchase units. A desired item may be sold as an individual item, in a bundle, in a pack, or in another verified grouped offer.
systems.availability: Current rotation details are shown only when a fresh authoritative offer snapshot exists.
actions: Inspect the verified purchase unit that contains a desired item when current evidence exists.
mechanics: Desired item identity and purchase-unit identity are separate.
Pricing and rotation are time-sensitive LiveOps data.
warnings: Wand fails closed on stale rotations and never assumes an item is individually purchasable.

systems.title: DreamSnaps
systems.summary: DreamSnaps is the game’s photo-challenge system. Wand keeps official in-game DreamSnaps information separate from Wand’s own Submit / Judge / Results / My DreamSnaps community event lifecycle.
systems.availability: Official challenge state is time-sensitive; Wand community events have their own publication and voting lifecycle.
actions: Create a qualifying photo in the game for official DreamSnaps.
Use Wand DreamSnaps surfaces for Wand-event submission, judging, results, and personal history when participating.
mechanics: Official results and Wand event results are distinct records.
warnings: Do not mix official competition status with Wand voting or rankings.

systems.title: Furniture and Decorating Mode
systems.summary: Furniture/Decorating Mode is the in-game system for placing, moving, rotating, and arranging supported world objects on editable grids.
systems.availability: What can be edited depends on the location, object type, progression state, and current game rules.
actions: Place and arrange supported decoration objects.
Use object and location information to understand where an item can be used.
mechanics: Not every visible world object is ordinary decoration. Roads, fences, Buildings, and progression-controlled objects can follow different rules.
warnings: If an object is fixed, progression-controlled, or otherwise unsupported, do not assume it can be moved or removed like furniture.

systems.title: Decoration Presets
systems.summary: Decoration Presets are reusable arrangements of decoration state. DDV native presets and Wand-native Presets are separate artifact systems.
systems.availability: Native preset capabilities depend on the game’s current preset implementation; Wand Presets use Wand’s own versioned artifact contract.
actions: Capture supported decoration selections into a preset.
Preflight a preset against the destination before applying it.
mechanics: Preset scope must preserve required descendants such as SubGrid content.
Road/Fence content is only included when the topology representation is proven safe for that preset operation.
warnings: Do not treat a DDV native preset as identical to a Wand Preset.

systems.title: Touch of Magic
systems.summary: Touch of Magic is DDV’s customization/design system for supported custom clothing and furniture. Wand treats ToM designs as a distinct reusable artifact/content type.
systems.availability: Creation and editing depend on the game’s supported customization surfaces and design data.
actions: Create or edit supported custom designs in game.
Use Wand ToM artifact features only for data shapes that the current codec validates.
mechanics: Customization.Design data is separate from ordinary catalog item identity.
warnings: Do not infer ownership or entitlement from a custom-design record.

systems.title: Crafting
systems.summary: Crafting converts required ingredients/resources into a defined recipe result using the game’s crafting recipe data.
systems.availability: A recipe must be available under the current game/save conditions before it can be crafted normally.
actions: Choose an available recipe and supply its required ingredients.
Use Wand item/recipe data to inspect canonical ingredients and results where present.
mechanics: Recipe identity and result-item identity are distinct database records even when Wand links them for display.
warnings: Do not infer current obtainability of an ingredient solely from recipe membership.

systems.title: Cooking
systems.summary: Cooking combines food ingredients at a cooking station into meal results defined by the current game data and recipe rules.
systems.availability: Cooking requires access to the relevant in-game cooking surface and ingredients.
actions: Select ingredients and cook a meal.
Use Wand recipe/item data to identify known canonical meal results where available.
mechanics: Quest-specific cooking ingredients can be special quest items and should not be generalized as normal ingredients.
warnings: Do not replace a Quest recipe with a guessed normal recipe when the Quest supplies special ingredients.

systems.title: Gardening
systems.summary: Gardening is the crop loop of planting seeds, watering crops, waiting for growth, and harvesting the resulting produce.
systems.availability: Seed/crop availability and growth behavior are item- and context-specific.
actions: Plant a seed in a valid gardening plot.
Water crops when required and harvest when mature.
mechanics: Crop and seed identities are linked but remain separate canonical items.
warnings: Exact growth times, yields, and biome modifiers are not generalized on this page without authoritative per-item data.

systems.title: Fishing
systems.summary: Fishing uses the Royal Fishing Rod at valid fishing locations and fishing spots to obtain fish and other fishing results.
systems.availability: Fishing targets depend on the current location, spot/state, and game conditions.
actions: Use the Royal Fishing Rod at a valid target and complete the in-game fishing interaction.
mechanics: Quest fishing targets may use dedicated quest interactions and should not be treated as ordinary fishing pools.
warnings: Do not infer a specific fish location or spawn rate without current source evidence.

systems.title: Mining
systems.summary: Mining uses the Royal Pickaxe on valid mining nodes and breakable world objects. Result tables and object restrictions are definition-driven.
systems.availability: Mineable nodes and breakable objects vary by world/biome and progression state.
actions: Use the Royal Pickaxe on supported nodes or breakables.
mechanics: Quest-only breakables can have progression semantics separate from ordinary mining nodes.
warnings: Do not treat every Pickaxe interaction as an ordinary resource node.

systems.title: Foraging
systems.summary: Foraging covers gathering supported naturally available world resources and harvestables outside the dedicated gardening/mining/fishing loops.
systems.availability: Resources depend on current world/biome, spawn state, and item definition.
actions: Collect available forage resources from the world.
mechanics: World-source provenance is recorded separately from inventory ownership.
warnings: Spawn location, quantity, and respawn timing are not generalized without exact evidence.

systems.title: Critter Feeding
systems.summary: Critter feeding is the interaction loop for wildlife/critters that can accept food and, under the game’s conditions, contribute to companion discovery/unlock state.
systems.availability: Eligible critters, approach behavior, and food preferences are critter-specific.
actions: Approach an eligible critter using its normal interaction pattern and feed a supported food.
mechanics: Critter state and Companion unlock state are related but not identical records.
warnings: Do not generalize favorite foods or approach rules across critter species.

systems.title: Villager Friendship
systems.summary: Friendship is character progression driven by supported interactions, gifts, quests, and other game-defined sources.
systems.availability: Friendship progression applies to supported villagers after their character/progression state is available.
actions: Interact with villagers through normal friendship-producing activities.
Use character Quest pages to follow friendship-quest progression.
mechanics: Friendship level/state and Quest progression are separate but related systems.
warnings: Exact XP values and daily limits are not generalized without source-backed tables.

systems.title: Hangout Roles and Bonuses
systems.summary: Hangout roles associate supported villagers with activity-related bonus behavior while hanging out.
systems.availability: Role assignment and bonus eligibility depend on character progression and current game rules.
actions: Assign/use a supported hangout role through the normal in-game character progression flow.
Hang out with the villager during the relevant activity.
mechanics: Role identity and friendship progression are distinct state.
warnings: Do not claim exact bonus probability or yield without current authoritative numeric evidence.

systems.title: Character and Realm Unlocks
systems.summary: Realms are dedicated spaces used to introduce or progress supported characters and Realm-specific Quests.
systems.availability: Realm/character unlock requirements are specific to each Realm and current progression.
actions: Enter an unlocked Realm through the supported game route.
Complete its Realm Quests to progress the associated character story.
mechanics: Realm identity, character unlock state, and Quest completion are separate canonical states.
warnings: Do not generalize one Realm’s cost or prerequisite to another.

systems.title: Biome and World Access
systems.summary: World access controls which Valley biomes, expansion worlds, and other supported outdoor locations the player can enter.
systems.availability: Access is progression- and content-specific and is represented by current world/location definitions and save state.
actions: Unlock/access locations through their normal in-game progression requirements.
mechanics: World, Biome, Area, and Floating Island identities are distinct and must not be collapsed into one location type.
warnings: Wand does not fabricate Area/Village identity for direct-root locations.

systems.title: Royal Tools and Upgrades
systems.summary: Royal Tools provide core world interactions such as digging, mining, fishing, watering, and other tool-specific actions. Upgrades can widen what a tool can interact with.
systems.availability: Individual tools/upgrades are unlocked through their specific progression sources.
actions: Use the appropriate Royal Tool on a supported world target.
mechanics: Tool capability is operation- and target-specific; a tool’s existence does not make every matching-looking world object editable.
warnings: Progression objects may use Royal Tool interactions but still require Quest-specific semantics.

systems.title: Fast Travel and Wishing Wells
systems.summary: Fast travel moves the player between supported unlocked travel destinations, including Wishing Well destinations represented by the current world/progression state.
systems.availability: A destination must be available/unlocked under current game rules before it is a valid travel target.
actions: Use the game’s fast-travel interface or supported Wishing Well interaction to travel between available destinations.
mechanics: Travel destination identity is distinct from arbitrary world-object placement.
warnings: Do not infer an unavailable destination from map presence alone.

systems.title: Player House and Rooms
systems.summary: The Player House combines Building progression with interior room state and therefore behaves differently from ordinary furniture.
systems.availability: Rooms and house-related capabilities depend on the current house and progression state.
actions: Use the house interface to access available rooms and house-related customization.
Treat room/interior state separately from ordinary outdoor furniture placement.
mechanics: Player House state can include progression-sensitive Building data in addition to placed decoration.
warnings: Do not assume every house element follows the same placement/removal rules as ordinary furniture.

systems.title: Companions
systems.summary: Companions are collectible/equippable follower entities represented separately from ordinary inventory items and critter encounters.
systems.availability: Companion availability depends on its supported acquisition/unlock source.
actions: Equip an unlocked companion through the game’s supported companion surface.
mechanics: Companion collected/unlocked state is derived from companion-specific data rather than generic stack quantity.
warnings: Do not infer a companion unlock from merely seeing the related critter.

systems.title: Photo Mode
systems.summary: Photo Mode is the game’s screenshot/composition system and the capture surface used by features such as DreamSnaps. Current v1.25 data includes expanding photo-mode capabilities such as pose-related definitions.
systems.availability: Photo options depend on the current game version, context, and unlocked features.
actions: Open Photo Mode, compose the scene, and use available camera/pose options.
mechanics: Photo-mode data is a distinct Collection/Guide concern and can expand between game versions.
warnings: Do not assume every internally defined photo option is unlocked for every player.

systems.title: Multiplayer Valley Visits
systems.summary: Valley Visits are the game’s multiplayer visit flow for entering or hosting another player’s Valley under supported online rules.
systems.availability: Multiplayer availability depends on supported game/account/network conditions; local save evidence alone is not an online entitlement check.
actions: Use the game’s normal multiplayer/visit flow to host or join a supported Valley visit.
mechanics: Online session/entitlement state is intentionally separated from Wand local editing.
warnings: Wand must not treat authentication, entitlement, or online-session state as a normal local edit target.

systems.title: Floating Islands
systems.summary: Floating Islands are separate outdoor destinations with their own world/grid identity rather than ordinary Valley biomes or Areas.
systems.availability: An Island can be used when that destination is available in the current game/save state.
actions: Travel to an available Floating Island and decorate within that Island’s own space.
Use the Island identity when browsing or editing Island-specific decoration state.
mechanics: Floating Islands have their own location identity and bounds; they are not interchangeable with Village Areas.
warnings: Do not treat a Floating Island as if it were just another Valley biome.

systems.title: Mounts, Bonding, and Gear
systems.summary: Mounts are a separate player-facing entity/progression family with mount ownership/bonding/gear-related state represented in current v1.25 data.
systems.availability: Mount-related features depend on the relevant content/progression and the specific mount definition.
actions: Use the game’s supported mount surfaces for riding, bonding, and applicable gear management.
mechanics: Mount state is not generic furniture/inventory quantity state.
warnings: Do not generalize bonding values, gear slots, or unlock requirements without per-feature evidence.

systems.title: Expansion and Adventure Access
systems.summary: Expansions and adventure content add their own worlds, Quests, systems, and item sources.
systems.availability: Access depends on the relevant supported content and the platform/account entitlement that grants it.
actions: Use world, Quest, and item pages to see which content family or expansion they belong to.
mechanics: Content provenance and purchase entitlement are different facts: an item can be identified as expansion content without proving that a particular account owns the expansion.
warnings: Local save contents alone are not treated as proof of platform entitlement.

systems.title: Timebending
systems.summary: Timebending is the Royal Hourglass interaction system used in Eternity Isle content for locating timebending targets/resources and related progression.
systems.availability: It depends on access to the relevant expansion/progression and Royal Hourglass capability.
actions: Use the Royal Hourglass to locate and recover supported timebending targets.
mechanics: Quest-specific Hourglass targets can be distinct from normal resource collection.
warnings: Do not generalize exact loot tables or target locations without current source evidence.

systems.title: Scramblecoin
systems.summary: Scramblecoin is the board-game system represented by dedicated game data and player-facing progression/content.
systems.availability: Availability depends on the relevant character/content progression in the current game.
actions: Start a supported Scramblecoin match and play using the game’s board-game rules and available pieces.
mechanics: Scramblecoin pieces/progression are separate from ordinary furniture/inventory objects.
warnings: This page does not invent piece stats or opponent rules not present in the current authoritative basis.

systems.title: Snippets and Lorekeeper Tales
systems.summary: Snippets/Lorekeeper Tales are a collectible/progression system represented in current game data and tied to their own content flow.
systems.availability: Availability depends on the relevant story/content progression and current world access.
actions: Collect supported Snippets and use them through the associated Lorekeeper/Tale progression surface.
mechanics: Snippet collection state is distinct from generic item-stack ownership where the game models it separately.
warnings: Do not infer Tale completion from possession of an unrelated collectible.

systems.title: Daisy's Boutique Challenges
systems.summary: Daisy's Boutique Challenges are the game’s boutique/design challenge flow associated with Daisy and supported customization/decorating data.
systems.availability: Challenge availability and requirements are challenge/state-specific.
actions: Start an available Boutique Challenge and satisfy the displayed design requirements using supported items/designs.
mechanics: Boutique challenges are distinct from DreamSnaps and from free-form Touch of Magic creation.
warnings: Do not import DreamSnaps scoring/requirements into Boutique Challenges.

systems.title: Restaurant Orders
systems.summary: Restaurant Orders are character meal requests handled through supported restaurant gameplay and cooking systems.
systems.availability: Orders depend on current character/restaurant state and are not a fixed permanent list.
actions: Prepare the requested meal through Cooking and deliver/serve it through the restaurant interaction.
mechanics: Order state is distinct from the underlying meal recipe definition.
warnings: Do not assume an old order remains active after the game state changes.

systems.title: Campaign and Promo Codes
systems.summary: Campaign or promo codes are a redemption mechanic used when Gameloft provides an active code or campaign.
systems.availability: A code is usable only while its own current requirements and validity window are satisfied.
actions: Use an officially supplied current code through the supported in-game redemption flow when one is available.
mechanics: Wand treats the redemption mechanic separately from any list of currently active codes.
warnings: Community-reported, expired, or future/unverified codes are not presented as canonical active codes.

systems.title: Cloud Save and Cross-Save
systems.summary: Cloud Save/Cross-Save synchronizes supported game progress through online account/platform services and is separate from the local save file itself.
systems.availability: Support depends on platform, account, network service, and current game rules.
actions: Use the game’s supported account/cloud flow to synchronize progress on compatible platforms.
mechanics: A local save file and its online synchronization/account state are separate.
warnings: Possessing a local save does not by itself prove that cloud synchronization or cross-save is active.

systems.title: Currencies and Resources
systems.summary: DDV uses multiple currencies and resources, each with its own acquisition and spending rules.
systems.availability: A currency or resource is available according to its own content, progression, and source rules.
actions: Use the relevant activity, shop, Quest, event, or reward source for that resource.
mechanics: Ordinary local resources and premium/account-backed value do not share one universal ownership model.
warnings: Premium currency and purchase/account records should not be treated like ordinary local material quantities.

systems.title: Memories
systems.summary: Memories are collectible/reconstructable records and images that can also act as Quest clues. Current game data and save state distinguish Memory content from ordinary inventory items.
systems.availability: Individual Memories become available through their specific source/progression conditions.
actions: View unlocked Memories through the game’s Collection/Memory surfaces.
When a Quest explicitly references a Memory, use that image/text as the intended clue.
mechanics: Some Quest puzzles intentionally rely on the Memory image rather than a separate objective instruction.
warnings: Do not treat an internal Memory identifier as a user-facing clue without localized/canonical presentation.

systems.title: Mailbox and Rewards
systems.summary: The mailbox delivers supported messages/rewards through a game-managed claim flow. Mail content/reward state is distinct from generic inventory ownership.
systems.availability: Messages/rewards depend on their source, delivery conditions, and current account/save state.
actions: Open an available mailbox message and claim supported rewards through the normal game flow.
mechanics: A reward may become inventory/collection state only after the game processes the claim.
warnings: Do not synthesize mail, receipts, purchase grants, or entitlement-backed rewards through ordinary local editing.

systems.title: Premium and DLC Entitlements
systems.summary: Premium/DLC entitlement is the platform/account permission that grants access to purchased or account-provided premium content.
systems.availability: Entitlement is established by the supported platform/account service for that content.
actions: Use the platform/game account flow to obtain or restore access to purchased content.
mechanics: Local items or save references can identify content provenance, but they do not independently prove an account entitlement.
warnings: Do not treat local inventory or save flags as a substitute for the platform’s entitlement state.
